Shows on-screen controls when you are not using a physical controller.\n\nUse this to make touch or controller input feel closer to the way you play. Avoid changing it when controls already feel correct, since extreme values can make aiming, menus, or touch features harder to use.

Changes the size of the on-screen controls.\n\nUse this to make touch or controller input feel closer to the way you play. Avoid changing it when controls already feel correct, since extreme values can make aiming, menus, or touch features harder to use.

Changes how transparent the on-screen controls are.\n\nUse this to make touch or controller input feel closer to the way you play. Avoid changing it when controls already feel correct, since extreme values can make aiming, menus, or touch features harder to use.

Changes analog stick sensitivity.\n\nUse this to make touch or controller input feel closer to the way you play. Avoid changing it when controls already feel correct, since extreme values can make aiming, menus, or touch features harder to use.
Filters small stick movement near the center to reduce drift. Raise it if the camera or character moves by itself; lower it if aiming feels unresponsive.
Sets how far analog triggers must move before input is sent. Raise it for noisy triggers; lower it for racing or pressure-sensitive controls.
Remaps physical face buttons before they reach the emulator. Use this when your controller layout does not match PS3 Cross, Circle, Square, and Triangle placement.
Allows supported games to send vibration to a physical controller or, when fallback is enabled, to the Android device body.
Scales vibration intensity for gamepad rumble and device fallback.
Plays a short pulse using the current vibration strength and routing.
Vibrates the phone or handheld body when a physical controller is missing or does not expose a rumble motor.
Swaps left and right stick axes. Useful for games or controllers with unusual stick routing.
Flips horizontal stick movement for steering or camera controls.
Flips vertical stick movement for camera or aiming controls.

Choose between the system Vulkan driver and a custom driver.\n\nUse a custom driver mainly on compatible Adreno devices when the system Vulkan driver has graphical bugs or weak performance. Stay with the system driver on Mali, PowerVR, unknown GPUs, or whenever the custom driver causes crashes.

EmuCoreC brings PS3 emulation to Android with a focused mobile interface, local library management, and an RPCS3-based emulation core.
Open the EmuCoreC website for downloads, news, and project links.
View source code, report issues, and follow development on GitHub.
Chat with the community, share feedback, and get project updates.
Help development continue through Patreon membership.
See more Android apps from the developer.

Adds light Android haptic feedback when an on-screen button, D-pad direction, or analog stick is first pressed. This affects control feel only and does not change in-game rumble.
Controls the device vibration strength used for touch control haptics. Raise it if the tick is too subtle, or lower it for quieter handheld play.
Plays the same press-and-release haptic pair used by on-screen controls, so you can compare presets and tune strength before launching a game.

Soft uses a gentle press and a very light release. Balanced gives a clear press with a lighter release and is the default. Crisp uses the shortest, sharpest pair for precise taps. Strong uses deeper, longer pulses for phones with weaker vibration motors. The strength slider scales the selected feel.
Reverses up and down aiming motion.

Aim converts phone rotation speed into the right analog stick for camera control in shooters and automatically returns to center when the phone stops moving. Steering converts the phone’s held tilt into the left analog stick for racing games and calibrates the current angle as center when gameplay starts. The selected mode is used only while a game is running and requires the corresponding motion sensor.
Controls how strongly phone movement deflects the emulated analog stick. Per-game overrides are recommended because games use different camera and steering response curves.
Filters sensor noise and hand shake. Lower values react faster; higher values feel steadier but add a small amount of latency.
This device does not expose the motion sensor required by the selected mode.

Accurately processes PPU DCBZ instruction. In addition, when combined with Accurate SPU DMA, SPU PUT cache line accesses will be processed atomically.

Use accurate double-precision FMA instructions in PPU and SPU backends. While disabling it might give a decent performance boost if your CPU doesn\'t support FMA, it may also introduce subtle bugs that otherwise do not occur. You shouldn\'t disable it if your CPU supports FMA.

When enabled, PPU atomic operations will operate on entire cache line data, as opposed to a single 64bit block of memory when disabled. Numerical values control whether or not to enable the accurate version based on the atomic operation\'s length.
Accurately set FPCC Bits in PPU backends. If unsure, do not modify this setting.
Respect Non-Java Mode Bit values for vector ops in PPU backends. If unsure, do not modify this setting.
Accurately set Saturation Bit values in PPU backends. If unsure, do not modify this setting.
Accurately set NaN results in vector instructions in PPU backends. If unsure, do not modify this setting.
Forces RSX pauses on SPU MFC_GETLLAR and SPU MFC_PUTLLUC operations.

Allows the host GPU to synchronize with CELL directly. This incurs a performance penalty, but exposes the true state of GPU objects to the guest CPU. Can help eliminate visual noise and glitching at the cost of performance. Use with caution.

Higher values increase sharpness of textures on sloped surfaces at the cost of GPU resources. Modern GPUs can handle this setting just fine, even at 16x. Keep this on Automatic if you want to use the original setting used by a real PS3.
Leave this on 16:9 unless you have a 4:3 monitor.
Controls which avport is used to sample audio data from.
Target buffer duration in milliseconds. Higher values make the buffering algorithm\'s job easier, but may introduce noticeable audio latency.
Determines the sound format of RPCS3. Use \'Auto\' to let RPCS3 decide the best format based on the audio device and the emulated audio format.
Controls which device is used by audio backend.

Determines the sound format of the emulation. Configure this setting if you want to switch between stereo and surround sound. Changing these values requires a restart of the game. The manual setting will use your selected formats while the automatic setting will let the game choose from all available formats.

Determines the sound format of the emulation. Configure this setting if you want to switch between stereo and surround sound. Changing these values requires a restart of the game. The manual setting will use your selected formats while the automatic setting will let the game choose from all available formats.
Controls which PS3 audio API is used. Games use CellAudio, while VSH requires RSXAudio.
Cubeb uses a cross-platform approach and supports audio buffering, so it is the recommended option. If it\'s not available, FAudio could be used instead.
Allows pad and keyboard input while the game window is unfocused.
Interface IP Address to bind to. Only available in custom configurations.

Buzz! support. Select 1 or 2 controllers if the game requires Buzz! controllers and you don\'t have real controllers. Select Null if the game has support for DualShock or if you have real Buzz! controllers.
Select Qt Camera to use the default camera device of your operating system.
Flips the camera image either horizontally, vertically, or on both axes.
Select the camera that you want to use during gameplay.
Depending on the game, you may need to select a specific camera type.
Changes the scale of emulated system time. Affects software which uses system time to calculate things such as dynamic timesteps.

When this mode is on, SPU emulation prioritizes savestate compatibility, however, it may reduce performance slightly. When this mode is off, some games may not allow making a savestate and show an SPU pause error in the log.
Sets the time to be used within the console. This will be applied as an offset that tracks wall clock time. Can be reset to current wall clock time by clicking "Set to Now".
Uses 16-bit audio samples instead of default 32-bit floating point. Use with buggy audio drivers if you have no sound or completely broken sound.

Sets the 3D stereo rendering mode (only available in custom configurations with a default resolution of 720p). Anaglyph uses different colors for each eye, which can then be filtered with certain glasses. Side-by-Side is more commonly supported by VR viewer apps. Over-Under is closer to the native stereo output, but less commonly supported.

Sets the 3D stereo rendering mode (only available in custom configurations with a default resolution of 720p). Anaglyph uses different colors for each eye, which can then be filtered with certain glasses. Side-by-Side is more commonly supported by VR viewer apps. Over-Under is closer to the native stereo output, but less commonly supported.
Increases the amount of usable system memory to match a DECR console and more. Causes some software to behave differently than on retail hardware.
Enables the selected API\'s inbuilt debugging functionality. Will cause severe performance degradation especially with Vulkan. Only useful to developers. If unsure, don\'t use this option.
Provides a graphical overlay of various debugging information. If unsure, don\'t use this option.
Derive the MAC address from the PSID.

Force host memory management calls to be inlined instead of handled asynchronously. This can cause severe performance degradation and stuttering in some games. This option is only needed by developers to debug problems with texture cache memory protection.
Disables RSX FIFO optimizations completely. Draws are processed as they are received by the DMA puller.

Disables use of hardware-native color-space remapping formats such as _sRGB and _SNORM suffixes. Disabling this option increases accuracy compared to PS3 but can also introduce some noise due to how the software emulation works.
Disables Fast Math for MSL shaders, which may violate the IEEE 754 standard. Disabling it may fix some artifacts, especially on Apple GPUs, at the cost of performance.
Disables running occlusion queries. Minor to moderate performance boost. Might introduce issues with broken occlusion e.g missing geometry and extreme pop-in.
Disables the loading and saving of shaders from and to the shader cache in the data directory.
Disable SPU GETLLAR spin optimization. This can cause severe performance degradation and stuttering in many games. This option is only needed for a select number of games.
Disables the vertex cache. Might resolve missing or flickering graphics output. May degrade performance.
Disables all video output and PS3 graphical rendering. Its only use case is to evaluate performance on CELL for development.
Disables the custom Vulkan memory allocator and reverts to direct calls to VkAllocateMemory/VkFreeMemory.
DNS used to resolve hostnames by applications.

Controls how much time it takes for RSX to start processing after waking up by the Cell processor. Increasing wakeup delay improves stability, but very high values can lower RSX/GPU performance. It is recommended to adjust this in 20µs to 40µs increments until the best value for optimal stability is reached.
Saves all audio as a raw wave file. If unsure, leave this unchecked.
Required for some Homebrew or Game Mods. If unsure, do not use this option

Emulate depth comparison operations where desktop hardware behavior differs from PS3, usually EQUAL comparison modes. Fixes excessive shadow flickering and Z-fighting in some games. This is most obvious in some games where the Z prepass depth format is different from the rasterization depth format, a scenario that will never work out correctly on compliant desktop hardware.
Enables audio buffering, which reduces crackle/stutter but increases audio latency.
Enable connection to the Clans server. Only affects games supporting the Clans feature.
Enable SPU RdEventStat spin. This increases CPU usage, this setting is beneficial for high-threaded CPUs (12+) with select number of games.
Activate Feral Interactive\'s GameMode. This is a series of CPU and GPU optimizations and can potentially benefit game performance on some systems.
Required for some Homebrew. If unsure, do not use this option.
Enables time stretching - requires buffering to be enabled. Reduces crackle/stutter further, but may cause a very noticeable reduction in audio quality on slower CPUs.
Enable UPNP. This will automatically forward ports bound on 0.0.0.0 if your router has UPNP enabled.

The button used for enter/accept/confirm in system dialogs. Change this to use the Circle button instead, which is the default configuration on Japanese systems and in many Japanese games. In these cases having the cross button assigned can often lead to confusion.

Controls which fullscreen mode RPCS3 requests from drivers when using Vulkan renderer. Automatic will let the driver choose an appropriate mode, while the other options will hint the drivers on whether they should use exclusive or borderless fullscreen. Using Prefer borderless fullscreen option can help if you have issues with streaming RPCS3 gameplay or if your system incorrectly enables HDR mode when using fullscreen.
Automatically close RPCS3 when closing a game, or when a game closes itself.

"Fast" is the least accurate setting, RSX does not emulate atomic FIFO buffer. "Atomic" benefits stability greatly in many games with little performance penalty. "Atomic & Ordered" is the most accurate but it is the slowest and without much stability benefit in games.

Forces emulation of all blit and image manipulation operations on the CPU. Requires \'Write Color Buffers\' option to also be enabled in most cases to avoid missing graphics. Significantly degrades performance but is more accurate in some cases. This setting overrides the \'GPU texture scaling\' option.
Only useful when debugging differences in GPU hardware. Not necessary for average users. If unsure, don\'t use this option.

Forces MSAA to use the host GPU\'s resolve capabilities for all sampling operations. This option incurs a performance penalty as well as the risk of visual artifacts but can yield crisper visuals when MSAA is enabled.

Controls how RPCS3 resolves render targets where color and depth alias the same memory. Auto is recommended for most games. · Auto is the existing behavior, biased toward depth. · Prefer Color keeps the color binding when color-write is enabled and depth-write is not. Fixes missing geometry in some deferred renderers (e.g. Starhawk) at the cost of skipping depth test for that draw. · Prefer Depth is the same as Auto for now.

Off is the fastest option. Using the frame limiter will add extra overhead and slow down the game. However, some games will crash if the framerate is too high. PS3 native should only be used if Auto is not working correctly as it can introduce frame-pacing issues. Infinite adds a positive feedback loop which adds another vblank signal per frame allowing more games to be fps limitless. Experienced users with need of other frame limits should use the setting "Second Frame Limit" in the configuration file.
Control the sharpening strength applied by FidelityFX Super Resolution. Higher values will give sharper output but may introduce artifacts.

Guitar Hero Live (GHL) Guitar controller support. Select 1 or 2 controllers if the game requires GHL Guitar controllers and you don\'t have real guitar controllers. Select Null if the game has support for DualShock or if you have real guitar controllers. A real guitar controller can be used at the same time as an emulated guitar controller.
Force all texture transfer, scaling and conversion operations on the GPU. May cause texture corruption in some cases.
Obey RSX memory tiling configuration when writing GPU data to vm memory. This can fix graphics corruption observed when Read Color or Read Depth options are enabled.
Allows to hook some functions like \'memcpy\' replacing them with high-level implementations. May do nothing or break things. Experimental.
If set to Connected, RPCS3 will allow programs to use your internet connection.
Provides a graphical overlay with pad input values for player 1. This is only shown if the debug overlay is disabled. If unsure, don\'t use this option.
DNS Swap List. Only available in custom configurations.
Some games support native keyboard input. Basic will work in these cases.
Sets the used keyboard layout. Currently only US, Japanese and German layouts are fully supported at this moment.

Some games may fail to boot if the system language is not available in the game itself. Other games will switch language automatically to what is selected here. It is recommended leaving this on a language supported by the game.
The console region defines the license area of the PS3. Depending on the license area, some games may not work.

Automatically removes older files from disk cache on boot if it grows larger than the specified value. Games can use the cache folder to temporarily store data outside of system memory. It is not used for long-term storage.
This setting is only available in the global configuration.

Searches the game\'s directory and precompiles extra PPU and SPU modules during boot. If disabled, these modules will only be compiled when needed. Depending on the game, this might interrupt the gameplay unexpectedly and possibly frequently. Only disable this if you want to get ingame more quickly.
Locks the native overlay input to the first player.
Dump game shaders to file. Only useful to developers. If unsure, don\'t use this option.
Controls the overall volume of the emulation. Values above 100% might reduce the audio quality.

Automatically removes older files from disk cache on boot if it grows larger than the specified value. Games can use the cache folder to temporarily store data outside of system memory. It is not used for long-term storage.
This setting is only available in the global configuration.

Limits the maximum number of threads used for the initial PPU and SPU module compilation. Lower this in order to increase performance of other open applications. The default uses all available threads.

Reduces CPU usage and power consumption, improving battery life on mobile devices. (0 means disabled) Higher values cause a more pronounced effect, but may cause audio or performance issues. A value of 50 or less is recommended. This option forces an FPS limit because it\'s active when framerate is stable. The lighter the game is on the hardware, the more power is saved by it. (until the preemption count barrier is reached)

Limits the maximum number of SPURS threads in each thread group. May improve performance in some cases, especially on systems with limited number of hardware threads. Limiting the number of threads is likely to cause crashes; it\'s recommended to keep this at the default value.

Forces delaying any odd MFC command, waits for at least 2 pending commands to execute them in a random order. Must be used with either SPU interpreters currently. Severely degrades performance! If unsure, don\'t use this option.
Creates MFC logs. Only useful to developers. Never use this.

Standard should be used for most games. SingStar emulates a SingStar device and should be used with SingStar games. Real SingStar should only be used with a REAL SingStar device with SingStar games. Rocksmith should be used with a Rocksmith dongle.

Standard should be used for most games. SingStar emulates a SingStar device and should be used with SingStar games. Real SingStar should only be used with a REAL SingStar device with SingStar games. Rocksmith should be used with a Rocksmith dongle.
Select up to 3 emulated MIDI devices and their types.

Only framebuffers greater than this size will be upscaled. Increasing this value might fix problems with missing graphics when upscaling, especially when Write Color Buffers is enabled. If unsure, don\'t change this option.

Enables mouse-based gyro emulation at game startup. It can also be toggled at any time with the associated hotkey. Hold the right mouse button to activate gyro input: moving the mouse maps to the X and Z motion axes, and the scroll wheel maps to the Y axis. Release the button to reset the motion values.
Provides a graphical overlay with mouse input values. This is only shown if the other debug overlays are disabled. If unsure, don\'t use this option.
Some games support native mouse input. Basic or Raw will work in these cases.
The PS Move handler is recommended for official PS Move controllers.
Emulate PS3 multisampling layout. Can fix some otherwise difficult to solve graphics glitches. Low to moderate performance hit depending on your GPU hardware.
Offloads some RSX operations to a secondary thread. Improves performance for high-core processors. May cause slowdown in weaker CPUs due to the extra worker thread load.
Currently only used for cellMusic emulation. Select Qt to use the default output device of your operating system. This may not be able to play all audio formats.

Affects maximum amount of PPU threads running concurrently, the value of 1 has very low compatibility with games. 2 is the default, if unsure do not modify this setting. Warning: changing this value invalidates the compiled PPU/SPU cache. The full module compilation will be repeated on the next launch.

Final image filtering. Nearest applies no filtering, Bilinear smooths the image, and FidelityFX Super Resolution enhances upscaled images. If the game is rendering at an internal resolution lower than your window resolution, FidelityFX will handle the upscale. FidelityFX can cause visual artifacts. FidelityFX does not work with stereo 3D output for now.
Shows all configured pads as always connected ingame even if they are physically disconnected.
Single-threaded: All pad handlers run on the same thread sequentially. Multi-threaded: Each pad handler has its own thread. Only use multi-threaded if you can spare the extra threads.

When enabled, opening the home menu will also pause emulation. While most games pause themselves while the home menu is shown, some do not. In that case it can be helpful to pause the emulation whenever the home menu is open.

Automatically pause emulation when RPCS3 loses its focus or the application is inactive in order to save power and reduce CPU usage. Do note that emulation pausing in general is not perfect and may not be compatible with all games. Although it currently also pauses gameplay, it is not recommended to rely on it as this behavior may be changed in the future and it is not the purpose of this setting.
Measure certain events and print a chart after the emulator is stopped. Don\'t enable if not asked to.
Centers the performance overlay horizontally and overrides the horizontal margin.
Centers the performance overlay vertically and overrides the vertical margin.
Controls the amount of information displayed on the performance overlay.
Enables or disables the performance overlay.
Shows the app, build and core version at the top, and the CPU and GPU rows at the bottom of the performance overlay.
Sets the font size of the performance overlay (measured in pixels).
Sets the amount of datapoints used in the framerate graph.
Controls the amount of information displayed on the performance overlay.
Enables or disables the framerate graph.
Sets the amount of datapoints used in the frametime graph.
Controls the amount of information displayed on the performance overlay.
Enables or disables the frametime graph.
Sets the horizontal distance to the screen border relative to the screen quadrant (measured in %).
Sets the vertical distance to the screen border relative to the screen quadrant (measured in %).
Sets the opacity of the performance overlay (measured in %).
Sets the on-screen position (quadrant) of the performance overlay.

Sets the time interval in which the performance overlay is being updated (measured in milliseconds). Setting this to 16 milliseconds will refresh the performance overlay at roughly 60Hz. The performance overlay refresh rate does not affect the frame graph statistics and can only be as fast as the current game allows.
Position overlay relative to the full window surface, enabling placement outside game\'s render area.
Play music during boot sequence if available.
Creates PPU logs. Only useful to developers. Never use this.

Recompiles and caches the game\'s PPU code using the LLVM Recompiler once before running it for the first time. This is by far the fastest option and should always be used. Should you face compatibility issues, fall back to one of the Interpreters and retry. If unsure, use this option.

Give PPUs an execution advantage when the SPUs are using reservations. This setting is recommended only for a few game for improving performance. DO NOT use it without being advised to due to potential performance degradation.
Fixup NaN results in vector instructions in PPU backends. If unsure, do not modify this setting.

Changes ZCULL report synchronization behaviour. Experiment to find the best option for your game. Approximate mode is recommended for most games. · Precise is the most accurate to PS3 behaviour. Required for accurate visuals in some titles such as Demon\'s Souls and The Darkness. · Approximate is a much faster way to generate occlusion data which may not always match what the PS3 would generate. Works well with most PS3 games. · Relaxed changes the synchronization method completely and can greatly improve performance in some games or completely break others.

Some SPU stages are sensitive to race conditions and allowing a limited number at a time helps alleviate performance stalls. Setting this to a smaller value might improve performance and reduce stuttering in some games. Leave this on auto if performance is negatively affected when setting a small value.

Prevent the display from sleeping while a game is running. This requires the org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver D-Bus service on Linux. This option will be disabled if the current platform does not support display sleep control.

If set to RPCN, RPCS3 will use the RPCN server as PSN connection if the game is supported. If set to Simulated, RPCS3 will try to fake the PSN connection, but any actual attempt at using the PSN functionality may result in errors or crashes. Simulated is only available in custom configurations.
Initializes render target memory using vm memory.
Initializes render target memory using vm memory.
Enables recording with overlays. This also affects screenshots.

Changes ZCULL report synchronization behaviour. Experiment to find the best option for your game. Approximate mode is recommended for most games. · Precise is the most accurate to PS3 behaviour. Required for accurate visuals in some titles such as Demon\'s Souls and The Darkness. · Approximate is a much faster way to generate occlusion data which may not always match what the PS3 would generate. Works well with most PS3 games. · Relaxed changes the synchronization method completely and can greatly improve performance in some games or completely break others.

Enables use of classic OpenGL buffers which allows capturing tools to work with RPCS3 e.g RenderDoc. Also allows Vulkan to use debug markers for nicer Renderdoc captures. If unsure, don\'t use this option.
Vulkan is recommended on Android. OpenGL uses the OpenGL ES compatibility backend and can help with game-specific graphics issues.

This setting will be ignored if the Resolution Scale is set to anything other than 100%! Leave this on 1280x720. Every PS3 game is compatible with this resolution. Only use 1920x1080 if the game supports it. Rarely due to emulation bugs some games will only render at low resolutions like 480p.

Scales the game\'s resolution by the given percentage. The base resolution is always 1280x720. Set this value to 100% if you want to use the normal Resolution options. Values below 100% will usually not improve performance.

Sets the 3D stereo rendering mode (only available in custom configurations with a default resolution of 720p). Anaglyph uses different colors for each eye, which can then be filtered with certain glasses. Side-by-Side is more commonly supported by VR viewer apps. Over-Under is closer to the native stereo output, but less commonly supported.
Loads the SDL GameController database for improved gamepad compatibility. Only used in the SDL pad handler.
Sets special MXCSR flags to debug errors in SSE operations. Accelerates PPU performance at the cost of accuracy.
Number of threads to use for the shader compiler backend. Only has an impact when shader mode is set to one of the asynchronous modes.
Changes the background image blur effect strength of the native shader loading dialog. This may be used to improve readability and/or aesthetics.
Changes the background image darkening effect strength of the native shader loading dialog. This may be used to improve readability and/or aesthetics.
Shows a background image during the native shader loading dialog/loading screen. By default the used image will be /PS3_GAME/PIC1.PNG.
This is the recommended option. If a shader is not found in the cache, nothing will be rendered for this shader until it has compiled. You may experience graphics pop-in.
Controls the precision level of generated shaders. Low precision generates much faster code depending on the hardware, but can sometimes generate minor visual glitches or flicker.
Shows analog limiter toggle hint using the native overlay.
Shows autosave/autoload hint using the native overlay.
Shows screenshot and recording hints using the native overlay.
Shows fatal error hints using the native overlay.
Shows mouse and keyboard toggle hint using the native overlay.
Shows the raw position of the PS Move input. This can be very helpful during calibration screens.
Shows \'Compiling PPU modules\' hint using the native overlay.
Shows pressure intensity toggle hint using the native overlay.
Shows \'Compiling shaders\' hint using the native overlay.
Show trophy pop-ups when a trophy is unlocked.
Stop writing any logs after game startup. Don\'t use unless you believe it\'s necessary.

Changes the sleep period accuracy. \'As Host\' uses default accuracy of the underlying operating system, while \'All Timers\' attempts to improve it. \'Usleep Only\' limits the adjustments to usleep syscall only. Can affect performance in unexpected ways.

This option controls the SPU analyser, particularly the size of compiled units. The Mega and Giga modes may improve performance by tying smaller units together, decreasing the number of compiled units but increasing their size. Use the Safe mode for maximum compatibility.

Recompiles and caches the game\'s SPU code using the LLVM Recompiler before running which adds extra start-up time. This is the fastest option with very good compatibility. If you experience issues, use the ASMJIT Recompiler.
Creates SPU logs. Only useful to developers. Never use this.

Recompiles and caches the game\'s SPU code using the LLVM Recompiler before running which adds extra start-up time. This is the fastest option with very good compatibility. If you experience issues, use the ASMJIT Recompiler.
Try to detect loop conditions in SPU kernels and use them as scheduling hints. Improves performance and reduces CPU usage. May cause severe audio stuttering in rare cases.
When enabled, SPU performance is measured at runtime. Enable only at a developer\'s request because when enabled it reduces performance a bit by itself.
Automatically puts the game window in fullscreen. Double click on the game window or press Alt+Enter to toggle fullscreen and windowed mode.
Leave this enabled unless you are a developer.
When this mode is on, savestates are loaded and paused on the first frame. This allows players to prepare for gameplay without being thrown into the action immediately.

Sets the 3D stereo rendering mode (only available in custom configurations with a default resolution of 720p). Anaglyph uses different colors for each eye, which can then be filtered with certain glasses. Side-by-Side is more commonly supported by VR viewer apps. Over-Under is closer to the native stereo output, but less commonly supported.

Sets the 3D stereo rendering mode (only available in custom configurations with a default resolution of 720p). Anaglyph uses different colors for each eye, which can then be filtered with certain glasses. Side-by-Side is more commonly supported by VR viewer apps. Over-Under is closer to the native stereo output, but less commonly supported.
Overrides the aspect ratio and stretches the image to the full display area.
Enforces strict compliance to the API specification. Might result in degraded performance in some games. Can resolve rare cases of missing graphics and flickering. If unsure, don\'t use this option.
Forces texture flushing even in situations where it is not necessary/correct. Known to cause visual artifacts, but useful for debugging certain texture cache issues.

When this mode is on, emulation exits when saving and the savestate file is concealed after its load, preventing reuse by RPCS3. This mode is like hibernation of emulation: if you don\'t want to be able to cheat using savestates when playing the game, consider using this mode. Do note that the savestate file is not gone completely, just ignored by RPCS3. You can manually relaunch it if needed.
Changes Texture sampling accuracy. (Small changes have a big effect.) Avoid using values outside the range of -12 to +12 if you\'re unsure. -3 to +3 is plenty for most usecases

Control how RPCS3 utilizes the threads of your system. Each option heavily depends on the game and on your CPU. It\'s recommended to try each option to find out which performs the best. Changing the thread scheduler is not supported on CPUs with less than 12 threads.
Buffer fill level (in percentage) below which time stretching will start.

DJ Hero Turntable controller support. Select 1 or 2 controllers if the game requires DJ Hero Turntable controllers and you don\'t have real turntable controllers. Select Null if the game has support for DualShock or if you have real turntable controllers. A real turntable controller can be used at the same time as an emulated turntable controller.

Enables use of native HUD within the game window that can interact with game controllers. When disabled, regular Qt dialogs are used instead. Currently, the on-screen keyboard only supports the English key layout.

When enabled, Vulkan will try to use PCI-e resizable bar address space for GPU uploads of timing-sensitive data. This yields a massive performance win on NVIDIA cards when the base framerate is low. For games with very high framerates, this option can result in worse performance for all GPU vendors.
Enables use of recursive scan on subfolders when scanning games from the selected folder. When disabled, games are scanned only on the selected folder.
Multiplies the rate of VBLANK by 1000/1001 for values like 59.94Hz. Known to fix the rhythm game Space Channel 5 Part 2
Adjusts the frequency of vertical blanking signals that the emulator sends. Affects timing of events which rely on these signals.

Enables vertical synchronization to eliminate tearing. Adaptive Mode - Prefers keeping up performance. It may skip frames or even tear to avoid reducing the game\'s framerate. Full Mode - No tearing allowed even if performance is reduced. This mode will by default limit your framerate to the display\'s refresh rate unless overriden in the driver control panel.
On multi GPU systems select which GPU to use in RPCS3 when using Vulkan. This is not needed when using OpenGL.

Determines how to schedule GPU async compute jobs when using asynchronous streaming. Use \'Safe\' mode for more spec compliant behavior at the cost of some CPU overhead. This setting works with all devices. Use \'Fast\' to use a faster but hacky version. This option is internally disabled for NVIDIA GPUs due to causing GPU hangs.

Stream textures to GPU in parallel with 3D rendering using asynchronous compute. Can improve performance on more powerful GPUs that have spare headroom. Only works with Vulkan renderer and greatly benefits from having MTRSX enabled if you have a capable CPU.
Configure the game window title. Changing this and/or adding the framerate may cause buggy or outdated recording software to not notice RPCS3.
Enable this option if you get missing graphics or broken lighting ingame. Might degrade performance and introduce stuttering in some cases. Required for Demon\'s Souls.
Writes depth buffer values to vm memory.
Control accuracy to SPU float vectors processing. Fixes bugs in various games at the cost of performance. This setting is only applied when SPU Decoder is set to Dynamic or LLVM.

Overrides the final display aspect ratio in thousandths (1778 = 16:9, 1333 = 4:3). Set it to 0 to use the game ratio. Use this only to fit unusual phone or tablet displays; an incorrect value stretches the image.

Absolute path to a RetroArch .slangp shader preset used when Output Scaling Mode is set to Shader chain. Leave it empty for normal output. Use only a compatible preset; an invalid path falls back to a plain image.
